Estimate study-level effect sizes

Source: R/effects.R
compute_effect_size.Rd

Calculates yi and sei with the same rules as bayesma's two-stage models:

Usage

compute_effect_size(
  data,
  measure = c("OR", "RR", "IRR", "MD", "SMD", "MedD"),
  ...,
  continuity = 0.5,
  design_effect = c("apply", "ignore")
)

Arguments

data

Outcome data frame in the canonical schema (see template_ma_data()).

measure

Effect measure.

...

Unused; must be empty.

continuity

Continuity correction for zero cells in binary and count outcomes.

design_effect

"apply" (default) uses effective sample sizes; "ignore" uses the reported sizes for every study.

Value

data with design_effect, n_int_eff, n_ctrl_eff, yi and sei columns added.

Details

  • "OR", "RR": event_* and n_*, with a continuity correction for zero (or, for RR, full) cells.

  • "IRR": event_* and person-time time_*.

  • "MD", "SMD" (Hedges' g): mean_*, sd_* and n_*.

  • "MedD": difference in medians by quantile estimation (McGrath et al., 2020) via metamedian, from whichever of minimum/median/maximum, quartiles, or mean/SD each arm reports.

Ratios are on the log scale. Rows lacking the required summaries get NA; for "MedD", a warning names the studies that cannot be estimated.

Clustered and crossover trials are handled with the design effect (see compute_design_effect()): sample sizes, events and person-time are divided by it before yi and sei are calculated. The reported n_int and n_ctrl are kept, so forest plots can show them; the effective sizes are added as n_int_eff and n_ctrl_eff. The design effect is always calculated from the design inputs (missing correlations give 1); a design_effect column already in data is replaced.
